parsed.faithful: 7. The husband, as the head of the wife, has the sole right of managing the goods in communion, which is called jus mariti. This right is so absolute, that it bears but little resemblance to a right of administering a common object. For the husband can, in virtue thereof, till, or even gift, at his pleasure, the whole goods falling under communion; and his creditors may affect them for the payment of his proper debts: for that the jus mariti carries all the characters of an affiliation, by the wife to her husband, of her movable effects. It arises ipso jure from the marriage; and therefore needs no other condition than. But a stranger may convey an effect to a wife, so as it shall not be subject to the husband's administration; or the husband himself may, in the marriage-contract, renounce his jus mariti in all or any part of his wife's movable effects.
